what: A dependency-free generic GGUF reader that opens and validates any GGUF file regardless of which architecture produced it. This is the foundation Deep2 lacked: it previously hardcoded DeepSeek-V2 shapes and a pre-generated op table, so it could not read a model outside that one family.
bugs_found_and_fixed: 32-bit file positioning: fseek/ftell use long, which is 32-bit on Windows, so any file above 2 GiB failed to open. Both probes above 900 MiB crashed with 0xC0000005 and the largest (25.4 GB) could not be measured. Fixed with _fseeki64/_ftelli64.

Iterator mixing across containers in blockIndices(): out.erase() was called with an iterator into a different vector, which is undefined behaviour. It produced a block count of 551009065816 for a 28-block model and crashed the caller.

Block-quantised sizes computed as nelements * type_size: Q8_0 was treated as 3 bytes per element. Q8_0 is block-quantised at 34 bytes per 32 elements, so five files including every expert-MoE model falsely reported tensors past end of file. Fixed with real block arithmetic for the legacy formats.

dtype_handling.size_unknown_deliberately: K-quants (Q2_K..Q6_K, Q8_K) and exotic types. The reader marks these unknown rather than guessing, so readRaw refuses instead of mis-reading, and the sweep counts them as unknown_size rather than validating them.
dtype_handling.readF32_support: F32, F16 and BF16 only. Quantised decoding is left to the kernel that owns the format, for example the Q4_K/Q6_K kernel in RAWRXD_DEEP2_GPU_QUANT_DOT_001. The tool reports readF32 does not decode Q5_0 rather than returning zeros silently.

notable_findings: qwen35 and qwen3next are also SSM-plus-MoE hybrids, so Mamba2 work is not Nemotron-specific.
gptoss uses ggml type 39 (MXFP4) for a large share of expert weights; this is outside the documented ggml type list and is reported as non-standard rather than mis-read.
deepseek4 has 256 experts with expert_weights_norm and expert_weights_scale 1.5, versus deepseek2 with 64 experts and scale 1.0.
nemotron_h (42 blocks, inner 7680, heads 96) matches the geometry the pre-existing untracked NemotronHGeometry.hpp targets, which is a different model from the nemotron_h_moe 53-block blob.
deepseek2 (27 blocks, 2048 embedding) is the family the existing ModelGenieExecutor implements, and appears once in this store as deepseek-coder-v2 16b.

what_this_does_not_establish: No model is executed. The reader opens, parses, validates offsets and reads tensor metadata, and nothing more.
No logits, tokens, TPS or parity result for any of these 56 models.
K-quant tensors have unvalidated byte ranges, which is 13,141 of 26,829 tensors in this store.
Supporting the file format is not the same as implementing an architecture. Inference still requires a per-architecture block plan, and sixteen of those do not exist yet.
next_steps: Add exact K-quant super-block sizes so the remaining 13,141 tensors can be range-validated.
Extend readF32 to decode the K-quant and legacy block formats so arbitrary tensors can be materialised.

Build per-architecture block plans on top of the reader, starting with the ones that share a family: llama, qwen2 and starcoder2 are all plain transformer-MLP; gemma3 and granite are close; deepseek2 and deepseek4 share MLA and MoE; nemotron_h, nemotron_h_moe, qwen35, qwen35moe and qwen3next share SSM-plus-MoE; gptoss and laguna are expert-MoE with non-standard dtypes.
